kept.name: Ariel semi-month exposure split
kept.note: Ariel's month partition, unconditional on price: long from the last trading day of the prior month through the Nth trading day of this one, then short (or flat) until the second-to-last session, flat for one day, repeat. Trading-day indices come from the session calendar -- weekday arithmetic with observed holidays removed -- so no price is used to place a session in its month. The daily hold is expressed as a state signal, which is what a rule with no exit event of its own has to be.
kept.source: Ariel, 'A Monthly Effect in Stock Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 18(1), 1987 - cited from the literature; not re-fetched this session (search budget exhausted). The exact split point (Ariel uses the last day of the prior month plus the first half of the month by trading-day count) is pinned to the 9th trading day here so the rule is unambiguous; sweep it.

kept.name: Consecutive Close-Above-Prior-High Exhaustion
kept.note: Counts consecutive bars whose close exceeds the PREVIOUS bar's high -- a strictly stiffer test than an up close, since the whole prior range was engulfed -- and shorts the first bar the streak reaches its threshold, optionally only beneath a 200 EMA. One entry per streak: the signal fires on the bar the counter crosses the threshold and never while it merely stays there. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low.
kept.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1601-1700/1601_Consecutive_Close_High1_Mean_Reversion -- 'counts consecutive closes above the prior high and sells once the count reaches a threshold; position exits when price falls below the prior low; optional 200 EMA filter'

kept.name: Rogers-Satchell Drift Detector
kept.note: Ratio of the UNdemeaned close-to-close variance (expectation sigma^2 + mu^2) to the Rogers-Satchell range variance (drift-free), so DR-1 estimates (drift/vol)^2 per bar with no smoothing constant. Trades in the direction of the N-bar return sum when DR clears the gate and the close is the extreme of the last few bars; exits when DR collapses back into the noise. From Rogers & Satchell (1991).
kept.source: Rogers & Satchell (1991), 'Estimating variance from high, low and closing prices', Annals of Applied Probability 1(4), 504-512 (the drift-independent estimator); Parkinson (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 61-65; Garman & Klass (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 67-78. Estimator comparison and formulas: https://portfoliooptimizer.io/blog/range-based-volatility-estimators-overview-and-examples-of-usage/ and https://macrosynergy.com/research/six-ways-to-estimate-realized-volatility/ . The drift-ratio construction itself is my synthesis from those estimators' bias properties.

kept.name: Bayesian Run-Length Collapse
kept.note: Runs Adams-MacKay Bayesian online change-point detection on log returns with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma conjugate prior, and trades the bar on which the MAP run length COLLAPSES instead of incrementing, gated on the posterior putting more than 30% of its mass on a run of five bars or fewer. Direction is read from the new segment, so the rule is agnostic between continuation and reversal.
kept.source: Adams & MacKay, 'Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection', arXiv:0710.3742 (2007) -- run-length posterior, message-passing recursion, constant hazard.

kept.name: Haircut Sharpe Position Sizing
kept.note: Ten ordinary candidate rules run side by side. At every recompute their expanding-window Sharpes become single-test t-stats and one-sided p-values, get adjusted for multiplicity by Bonferroni, Holm and BHY against a trial count of `trials`, are inverted back to a haircut Sharpe, and become a continuous weight w = clip(HSR/sr_target, 0, w_max); the traded signal is the sign of the w-weighted vote, so allocation moves continuously with multiple-testing-adjusted significance instead of switching on and off, and a rule whose w hits zero on retire_n consecutive recomputes is retired for good (retire_n=0 lets a rule come back). Sizing proper belongs to the harness, so the paper's risk fraction is expressed as the weight each rule carries in the vote. The trial count is swept over 4/10/40 rather than the paper's 100/578/5000: at intraday sample lengths a multiplicity of 100 haircuts every rule to zero and the family never trades at all, which is Harvey and Liu's point but produces no data.
kept.source: Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2015), 'Backtesting', Journal of Portfolio Management 42(1), 13-28 - the haircut Sharpe ratio and the exact Bonferroni / Holm / BHY adjusted p-value formulas, plus the finding that the haircut is non-linear and that the customary 50% haircut is too punitive for high-Sharpe and too lenient for low-Sharpe strategies. PDF: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.PDF . Companion: Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2014), 'Evaluating Trading Strategies', JPM 40(5), 108-118.

kept.name: Strong Close Into a New Low
kept.note: Shorts the bar that breaks to a new N-bar low and then closes in the top of its own range (IBS above threshold) -- a failed flush whose bounce is already spent by the close. Optional 200-EMA downtrend filter and an optional intraday session window given in UTC minutes-of-day. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low, which is a bar-versus-bar test rather than an indicator.
kept.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1501-1600/1598_10_Bar_Low_Pullback -- 'Low breaks the previous LowestPeriod bars lowest low; IBS > IbsThreshold (0.85); optional close below EMA200; exit on close below previous low'

kept.name: Bertram Cost-Aware OU Band Optimization
kept.note: SINGLE-SYMBOL ADAPTATION of a multi-symbol idea. The harness supplies one symbol, so the cointegrated second leg is replaced by the symbol's own trailing mean log price: x = log(C) - mean(log C, mu_win). Everything that makes the idea distinct is kept. An AR(1) fit of x gives theta = -log(rho) per bar and the stationary sd; entry a and exit m are then jointly chosen over a grid to maximise the RATE (m - a - cost)/E[T_cycle], with E[T] the exact OU first-passage time (pi^0.5/theta)*(F(w_m)-F(w_a)), F(w) = int_0^w e^(s^2)(1+erf s) ds, verified against the ODE it solves. The full cycle is a->m plus m->a, so capital's idle leg is paid for too. Bertram's Sharpe objective is not offered: at a zero risk-free rate it collapses to sqrt(E[T]/Var[T]), which is independent of the return per cycle and therefore ignores the cost term entirely - the rate objective is the one where cost bites. m* comes out well away from zero, which is the whole point.
kept.source: Bertram (2010), 'Analytic Solutions for Optimal Statistical Arbitrage Trading', Physica A 389(11); large-scale test with data-snooping controls in Cummins & Bucca (2012), 'Quantitative Spread Trading on Crude Oil and Refined Products Markets', Quantitative Finance. Trade-cycle decomposition T = T1 + T2 and the return function r(a,m,c) = m - a - c reproduced from Krauss (2015), FAU Discussion Paper 09/2015, section 4.2 (equations 22-24).

kept.name: Net-Edge Admission Gate
kept.note: Gates a signal on cost rather than on strength. When the base rule fires (close crossing its EMA) three quantities are formed: the AGK EDGE effective-spread estimate over the trailing est_win OHLC bars as a fraction of price, with the Roll half-spread doubled as the fallback when EDGE is undefined; a square-root impact term y_imp*sigma_20*sqrt(Q/V20); and the conditional expected edge, the median forward h_bars log return over every past bar in the trailing edge_look window on which this same signal fired in this same direction, counting only fires at least h_bars old so the outcome was already observable. The trade is admitted only if the expected edge clears hurdle times the round trip, so the identical signal is accepted on a liquid name and refused on an illiquid one at the same dollar size. Cost enters the entry condition, not the P&L accounting.
kept.source: Ardia, D., Guidotti, E., Kroencke, T.A. (2024), 'Efficient Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Open, High, Low, and Close Prices', Journal of Financial Economics 161:103916 (reference implementation at github.com/eguidotti/bidask); Roll (1984) as restated in Novy-Marx & Velikov, 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), p.4; Toth et al. (2011) square-root law for the impact term.

kept.name: Gap-Cadence Event Calendar Run-In
kept.note: Reconstructs a recurring event calendar from the symbol's OWN bars: take the largest |open/prev-close - 1| jumps in a trailing window, keep the longest subset whose consecutive spacings all fall inside an admissible band, and forecast the next event at last + median spacing. Go long from entry_off bars before that forecast and exit exit_off bars before it -- always flat across the event itself. Self-falsifying: a forecast date that passes without a jump of stale_mult times the typical detected-event jump retires the symbol until a new event is observed. Spacings are in BARS, not sessions, because the probe data is far shorter than a quarterly cycle; on daily bars the band should be set to the 55-70 session spacing the source specifies, and the staleness reference is the median jump of the events the fit itself found rather than a 250-session median. Candidates are chosen with non-maximum suppression (min_sep bars apart, defaulting to half the low end of the spacing band) so that one violent event cannot occupy several candidate slots with its own neighbouring bars -- the source picks the 12 largest gap SESSIONS, which are distinct by construction.
kept.source: Beaver (1968) on announcement-period return variance and trading volume, cited in Kothari & Warner (2006) footnote 1. Frazzini & Lamont (2007) 'The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume' (NBER WP 13090) for the run-in premium. The gap-cadence reconstruction device itself is a synthesis -- no earnings calendar is available on this feed, so the event dates are inferred from the periodicity of the symbol's own overnight gaps, and the estimator is falsifiable.

kept.name: Amihud Illiquidity Reversal
kept.note: Bar-based Amihud lambda: rolling mean of |log return| / dollar volume. Buys when that ratio sits above its own trailing percentile AND price is more than atr_d ATRs below its 20-bar mean -- a decline produced by very little money changing hands. Exits when the ratio falls back under its trailing median, or price reclaims the mean, or the clock runs out. The percentile is a true rolling rank over the trailing window, not a fixed cut.
kept.source: Bar-based Amihud lambda, AFML pp.288-289, implemented as get_bar_based_amihud_lambda in mlfinlab/microstructural_features/second_generation.py - source read from the archived mlfinlab-master.zip at https://github.com/mnewls/MLFINLAB.

kept.name: No Supply No Demand Bar
kept.note: Volume Spread Analysis read of an ABSENCE of participation: a narrow-range bar whose volume undercuts each of the previous two bars, closing in the half of its range that contradicts its own direction, taken only in the matching side of the SMA. Mandatory confirmation on the very next bar (close through the signal bar's extreme on higher volume) turns the qualitative read into a rule.
kept.source: Tom Williams, 'Master the Markets' (Volume Spread Analysis). Operational definition -- up/down bar, narrow spread, volume lower than the previous two bars, close position within the bar, confirming next bar on rising volume -- from tradingsetupsreview.com's VSA guide and atas.net's no-demand/no-supply article. 'Narrow spread' is undefined in both sources and is pinned here to a fraction of the mean range of the five bars before the signal bar.

kept.name: Naked POC Magnet
kept.note: A real volume-at-price profile is built for each regular-hours session: bins bin_pct percent of the session open wide, every bar's volume spread evenly over the bins its [low, high] covers, and the POC is the midpoint of the fullest bin. A finished session's POC joins a list and stays on it only while it remains NAKED - the moment any later session's range contains that price it is struck off, so membership is a topological fact about the tape rather than a threshold. Between start_min and end_min ET the nearest naked POC above and below the last price are measured in units of the SESSION ATR(14) built from the same profiles; the setup trades toward whichever is nearer, provided it sits between min_atr and max_atr away - close enough to be reachable, far enough to be worth the trip. One trade per level per day. Exit is the level itself, or flat at flat_min ET. The 1.0 x session-ATR stop the idea specifies is carried as st_atr in BAR-ATR units, which is the only stop unit the shared harness has.
kept.source: Market Profile / volume profile lineage (Steidlmayer, CBOT Liquidity Data Bank). Definitions and the naked/virgin POC concept per LuxAlgo concept library, https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/naked-poc/ and https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/point-of-control/ ; profile construction per TradingView docs, https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000502040-volume-profile-indicators-basic-concepts/ . Exact bin widths, ATR gating and the 60-session horizon are the harvesting agent's specification.

cut.name: Weis Wave swing volume divergence
cut.note: Segments price into waves with an ATR zigzag on the close, then compares each completed leg with the previous leg in the same direction: same ground covered (travel >= previous) on materially less volume (wave volume <= 0.70x) is Wyckoff effort-versus-result at swing scale, so the leg is faded. Holding period is measured in waves - the trade is closed when the next wave running in its direction completes.
cut.source: David Weis's Weis Wave, a computerisation of the wave charts in Wyckoff's course; see Weis, 'Trades About to Happen' (Wiley, 2013). The harvester could not retrieve a primary page for the construction and pinned the wave definition to a 2.0-ATR zigzag itself; that segmentation is the harvester's choice, not Weis's.

cut.name: Turn-of-Month Flow Window
cut.note: Pure calendar: long from the close of the second-to-last weekday session of the month through the close of the third session of the new month, with no indicator condition. Optional skip when the previous session's ATR/close sits above the 90th percentile of its own trailing history. McConnell & Xu's four-day turn-of-month window.
cut.source: John J. McConnell and Wei Xu, 'Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month', Financial Analysts Journal 64(2), 2008 - trading rules and magnitude VERIFIED via https://quantpedia.com/strategies/turn-of-the-month-in-equity-indexes/, which specifies 'Buy SPY ETF 1 day (some papers say 4 days) before the end of the month and sell the 3rd trading day of the new month at the close'. Mechanism: Ogden (1990) on standardised payment dates; Lakonishok and Smidt (1988) on calendar anomalies.

cut.name: Kyle Lambda Shock
cut.note: Estimates Kyle's price-impact coefficient lambda as the rolling OLS slope of log returns on signed square-root dollar volume, then trades the direction of a large bar that occurs while lambda is both unusually high (z >= 2) and still rising -- the signature of a book that has thinned out ahead of a directional repricing.
cut.source: Kyle (1985), Econometrica 53(6); estimation form (returns on signed sqrt dollar volume, rolling window) from OFR Working Paper 15-11, 'Systemwide Commonalities in Market Liquidity', and Hasbrouck (2009).

cut.name: Levered ETF close rebalance drift
cut.note: A daily-reset levered or inverse ETF must finish the session holding its multiple times the new NAV, so the required trade is always in the same direction as the day's move, scales with (L^2 - L) * AUM * return, and has to be done near the close. This measures the session move R against the symbol's own recent daily sigma at a bar trig_min minutes before the close and goes WITH the move when |R| > k_sig * sigma, flattening at the close (leg 1); leg2=1 then takes the opposite side into the next session's open to collect the give-back once the mechanical demand stops. The session close is located from the tape - the heaviest-volume bar in the back half of the session, medianed over the previous slot_days sessions - so no timezone table is needed and a DST shift is followed automatically. TWO HONEST DEPARTURES from the idea as written: R is measured on the traded symbol itself rather than on SPY, because a single-symbol harness cannot read another ticker (the same mechanism applies to any underlying with levered products on it), and leg 2 fills at the first bar after the close rather than at the official 16:00 print, because the runner always fills at the next bar's open.
cut.source: Synthesis of a documented mechanism. Cheng & Madhavan, 'The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds' (Barclays Global Investors, 2009), derive the (leverage^2 - leverage) x AUM x return rebalancing formula and its end-of-day concentration; also the subject of SEC/FINRA investor alerts on leveraged ETFs. The idea's author could not re-fetch these in their session, so the thresholds and the two-leg structure are their construction on top of the published mechanics, not a rule lifted from a paper.
cut.cut_reason: profitable on only 57% of the symbols it scored on

cut.name: Fractionally differenced z-score
cut.note: Lopez de Prado fractional differencing of log close. The weight recursion w_k = -w_{k-1}*(d-k+1)/k is truncated at |w_k| < tol; d is the SMALLEST value on the {0, 0.05, ... 1.00} grid at which an augmented Dickey-Fuller test on the transformed series rejects the unit root at 95%, fitted once on the leading in-sample block and then held fixed. Trades fresh crossings of a +/- z threshold on the standardised series. NOTE ON THE TRUNCATION THRESHOLD: the source specifies 1e-5, which on these sample lengths demands 2000-4000 taps - longer than the usable history, so every low d would be skipped and the 'smallest d' would be decided by the window length rather than by the data. tol is therefore swept at 1e-3/1e-4; 1e-4 needs ~500 taps and retains ~95% of the total weight mass. On the probe symbols the ADF t-statistic is strictly monotone in d, so the upward scan finds a genuine minimum, and the selected d differs by symbol (0.10 to 0.25).
cut.source: Lopez de Prado, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning', ch.5 sections 5.4.2 and 5.5 (pp.78-83), implemented as FractionalDifferentiation.get_weights and frac_diff in mlfinlab/features/fracdiff.py, with the exact recursion weights_ = -weights[-1]*(diff_amt - k + 1)/k and the threshold-based truncation - source read from the archived mlfinlab-master.zip at https://github.com/mnewls/MLFINLAB. Referenced there to Hosking (1981), https://wwwf.imperial.ac.uk/~ejm/M3S8/Problems/hosking81.pdf

cut.name: Developing POC Ratchet
cut.note: Builds the DEVELOPING volume-at-price profile inside each RTH session, rows 0.05 daily ATR wide, and records the developing point of control at every 30-minute period close. Goes long when the POC has ratcheted monotonically up for `runs` consecutive periods, has travelled at least mig*ATRd in total (strict=1 additionally demands a move in every single period, which real developing POCs rarely deliver), has never printed below the base of the ratchet at any earlier period today, and price is above it; short is the exact mirror. One entry per session, none before 11:00 or after 14:00 ET. The exit is the idea's other half: the stop starts at the base of the ratchet and then TRAILS ON THE DEVELOPING POC ITSELF, checked only at period closes, flat by 15:55. The session clock is derived with utc_offset (4 = EDT; set 5 for winter data).
cut.source: Developing POC / developing value area is standard Market Profile instrumentation (Steidlmayer, CBOT Market Profile; Dalton et al., 'Mind Over Markets'), and Sierra Chart documents 'Volume Point Of Control For Bars' and developing value-area studies as built-in tools. The monotone-ratchet predicate, the migration-distance gate and the POC-trailing exit are the harvester's quantification (synthesis).
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Netted Value-Momentum Combination
cut.note: Two rank signals at deliberately opposite horizons on one symbol -- a long-horizon VALUE measure (today's price against a price average lifted from deep in the past) and a 2-to-12-month style MOMENTUM measure that skips the freshest window -- each converted to a percentile rank and NETTED into a single weight before any order exists. Cheap-and-rising gets roughly double weight; cheap-but-still-falling cancels to inside the no-trade band and is never traded. AMP rank the cross-section of an ETF universe; this feed is single-symbol, so the rank is against the measure's own trailing history instead, which keeps the netting structure and the opposite horizons and drops only the cross-sectional part. Horizons are in BARS, scaled so value stays several times longer than momentum.
cut.source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen, 'Value and Momentum Everywhere' (Journal of Finance 2013), equation (3): r_COMBO = 0.5*r_VALUE + 0.5*r_MOM; equation (1) for rank weights; p. 938 for the 5-year value proxy and the choice of MOM2-12 as the momentum measure (the paper explicitly defends 2-12 over 7-12, citing Novy-Marx 2012 and Goyal & Wahal 2012).

cut.name: Stambaugh-Corrected Augmented Predictive Regression
cut.note: Bars are aggregated into blocks; a persistent OHLCV predictor (log price/moving average, log realised volatility, or log Amihud illiquidity) is fitted with its own AR(1), the persistence is de-biased with Kendall's small-sample correction, the corrected innovation is put on the right-hand side of the predictive regression as an extra regressor, and only then is the slope used. Long only while the bias-corrected slope has the expected sign AND its Newey-West t-statistic clears the gate AND the forecast is positive -- so the entry condition is a property of the ESTIMATOR, not of the price, and the exit is the slope losing its significance. Monthly rebalancing becomes one decision per block.
cut.source: Stambaugh, R.F., 'Predictive regressions', Journal of Financial Economics 54, 1999 -- the canonical statement of the bias. The implementation is taken from Amihud, Y., 'Illiquidity and Stock Returns', NYU working paper FIN-00-041 (JFM 5, 2002), pp.19-20, where the Kendall (1954) correction, the appeal to Stambaugh (1999) and the augmented model (11) with the AR residual on the right-hand side are all set out. Newey-West lag alternatives and the wild-bootstrap substitute are named in Neely et al., FRB St. Louis WP 2010-008, p.5.
cut.cut_reason: profitable on only 50% of the symbols it scored on

cut.name: Tug-of-War Session Split
cut.note: Holds the same signal in one session and only one. S = close above EMA(ema_n) with ADX(14) >= adx_min, read at the last regular-hours bar of the day. arm=0 (overnight) buys at that closing bar and exits at the next regular-session open, carrying zero intraday exposure; arm=1 (intraday) buys at the regular-session open and exits at that day's close, carrying zero overnight exposure. Neither arm has a stop, target or trail - the session boundary IS the exit, which is the whole point of the test. The signal and its parameters are identical across arms so the only difference is which half of the day the exposure is held in.
cut.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019), 'A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134:192-213 (personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/tugofwar.pdf).

cut.name: Campbell-Yogo Bonferroni Q Predictor Gate
cut.note: A licensing test that decides, every re-evaluation, whether a persistent predictor is allowed to drive exposure at all. The predictor under test is x = log(close / SMA(close, pw)), the log gap between price and its own long moving average: OHLCV-only, highly persistent, and with an innovation almost perfectly correlated with the return innovation -- exactly the configuration in which a naive t-test on beta is really a 15-20 percent test. Its prior sign is POSITIVE and is fixed before the data is seen: over horizons of days, time-series momentum says price above its own long average predicts continuation, and the opposite value/reversion prior belongs to multi-year horizons that no bar count here reaches. Each re-evaluation the DF-GLS statistic is computed on x and INVERTED to a confidence set for rho, then for each retained rho the paper's Q-statistic gives a confidence interval for beta, and the Bonferroni interval is the union of those. Exposure is taken only while that whole interval lies strictly above zero; the moment it admits zero the predictor is unlicensed and exposure falls back to flat, this harness's version of the prevailing-mean benchmark weight. No stop and no target, per the idea. Three implementation notes, stated plainly. (1) The DF-GLS null bands are read from a lookup table over c = T(1 - rho), simulated once offline at T = 250 with 5,000 Gaussian paths and embedded in the code at three Bonferroni splits alpha1 = 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.30 -- reading the interval for c off a table is exactly what the paper does with the Elliott-Rothenberg-Stock tables, and re-simulating 5,000 paths per rho per period would burn the study's wall clock to reproduce a constant. (2) Q is LINEAR in beta0, so the |Q| < zq retention set is solved in closed form instead of searched over a beta grid; the answer is identical and it costs nothing. (3) The test is re-run every reeval periods rather than at every period end, which is the one O(T) cost the study cannot afford at every bar; nothing else about the test changes. Timeframe map: 'daily bars aggregated to monthly, monthly re-evaluation' becomes agg bars to a period on an expanding sample, which is what the paper itself uses.
cut.source: Campbell, J.Y. and Yogo, M., 'Efficient Tests of Stock Return Predictability', NBER Working Paper 10026 (Oct 2003), published JFE 81, 2006 - read directly at https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w10026/w10026.pdf. The Q-statistic is eq. (9) on p.8; the local-to-unity framework is section 3.1; the use of DF-GLS (Elliott, Rothenberg and Stock) rather than ADF to build the confidence interval for c, and the reason for it, are on pp.523-527 of the text; the Bonferroni construction and the choice of the Q-test over the Bonferroni t-test of Cavanagh, Elliott and Stock (1995) are in section 3.3. The simulation-based inversion of the DF-GLS statistic over a rho grid is my pinning-down of a step the paper implements via published lookup tables.

cut.name: Range-Bar Flip Count Regime
cut.note: Range bars of fixed height S = s_atr * ATR(atr_n), S recomputed at the first regular-hours bar of each session and then frozen for that session. A range bar opens at the previous one's close and closes as soon as its running high minus running low reaches S; because only OHLC is available and not the path inside a bar, the extreme reached LAST is taken to be the high when that bar closed up and the low when it closed down. F is the number of direction flips among the last flip_win closed range bars -- a unit-free path-efficiency measure, since the price distance per bar is constant by construction, which is exactly what ADX and the choppiness index cannot claim on time bars. Enter with the tape when F <= in_flip and the last run_len range bars all closed the same way; exit on the same statistic at a looser threshold (F >= out_flip), on opp_run range bars against the position, or after rb_max range bars. The 2*S hard stop is 2*s_atr in ATR units, left to the shared execution grid whose stops bracket it. One approximation is worth naming: a single 5-minute bar wide enough to complete more than one range bar closes only one, because the path inside that bar is unknown and inventing the rest would be inventing data.
cut.source: Range-bar construction is standard in futures platform documentation (constant-range bars); the flip-count statistic and the entry/exit thresholds are my synthesis. The path-efficiency reasoning follows Kaufman's efficiency ratio (Perry Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods', Wiley) applied in range-bar space rather than time space.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: ARCH-LM Clustering Gate
cut.note: Runs Engle's Lagrange-multiplier test for ARCH effects on a rolling window of the symbol's own log returns (auxiliary OLS of squared demeaned returns on five of their own lags, LM = m*R^2, chi-square(5)). A range-expansion bar is then traded WITH its direction when the test proves volatility clusters, and AGAINST it when the test says it does not -- the specification test picks the side rather than filtering the setup.
cut.source: Engle (1982), 'Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity with Estimates of the Variance of United Kingdom Inflation', Econometrica 50(4) - the LM test, T*R^2 from the auxiliary regression of squared residuals on their own lags. Chi-square critical values are standard table values; the two-branch regime switch is the harvested idea's synthesis.
cut.cut_reason: profitable on only 58% of the symbols it scored on

cut.name: Own-Footprint Decay Gate
cut.note: A propagator-model cooldown: every fill of our own leaves a residual footprint sigma*(q/V)^psi that decays as (1+lag)^-beta, and no new entry fires until the signed sum of those footprints has decayed below theta_foot * the 20-bar per-bar return stdev. The base signal it gates is a plain N-bar breakout, so what is being measured is the gate. theta_foot is swept below the paper's 0.1-0.5 band because 100-share slices against five-minute bar volume produce a footprint of order 0.01-0.05, where the published band would leave the gate permanently open.
cut.source: Bouchaud, J-P. (2009), 'Price Impact' (arXiv:0903.2428): propagator p_T = p_-inf + lambda * SUM G(N-n) eps_n v_n^psi with G(l) ~ l^-beta, beta = (1-gamma)/2 ~ 0.25, and the BARRA-style response R(dt,v) = A sigma sqrt(v/V). Motivated by Gatheral (2010), 'No-Dynamic-Arbitrage and Market Impact', Quantitative Finance 10(7); decay level sanity-checked against Zarinelli, Treccani, Farmer & Lillo (2014, arXiv:1412.2152).

cut.name: Net-the-book internal crossing
cut.note: A pre-trade rule sitting in front of a book of K signals that share one ticker. Instead of sending each signal's desired change d_k, the book computes the NET D = sum_k d_k and the GROSS Gr = sum_k |d_k| and sends only D, so signals trading against each other inside the book cross for free instead of paying two round trips to end up flat. Two things then decide whether even D goes. BAND: suppressed unless the trade notional exceeds max(min_ticket, k_band * c^(1/3) * |current position notional|), with c an Abdi-Ranaldo close-high-low effective spread (the estimator EDGE generalises) plus a square-root impact term on the trade's own size against rolling dollar volume. MARGIN RULE: a net sell while at least one signal still wants to be long is slowed by `slow`, and symmetrically for a net buy against a standing short view - Novy-Marx and Velikov's screens, the mechanism by which a second strategy is taken on at effectively negative transaction cost. The surviving delta moves the book position P and the traded direction is sign(P) once |P| clears pos_min. k_band = 0 with slow = 1.0 and rebal = 1 is the un-netted control, plain sign-of-the-vote, so the sweep measures the rule against its own absence rather than only against itself. The internalisation ratio 1 - sum|D| / sum Gr is computed and written to the run log as the idea asks. WHAT IS NOT HERE, stated plainly: this harness gives a family one symbol and a fixed share size. D_i, Gr_i, band_i and the margin rule are all per-ticker in the source and survive intact, but the cross-ticker portfolio-risk bypass has nothing to act on, and a netted delta can only express itself as a change of DIRECTION rather than a change of size - so what is measured here is the turnover the netting and the band remove, which the harness does charge for on every fill, not the full share-level internalisation of a real multi-ticker book. The per-ticker stop bypass is the harness ATR stop, which liquidates in full and ignores both the band and the margin rule, exactly as specified.
cut.source: Novy-Marx, R. & Velikov, M., 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), section 6 'Alternative Cost Mitigation Strategies': 'an alternative cost mitigation technique that allows investors trading one strategy to opportunistically take small positions in another at effectively negative trading costs. We call this technique trading one strategy on the margin of another, but it is also known in the industry as screens or filters. The screened strategies are enhanced by slowing sales (purchases) and short covers (shorts) when the screening variable is in the top (bottom) x%.' Spread estimator: Abdi & Ranaldo (2017), 'A Simple Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily Close, High, and Low Prices', RFS 30(12), which Ardia, Guidolin & Kazak's EDGE generalises.

cut.name: Volume-conditioned momentum life cycle
cut.note: Lee & Swaminathan's momentum life cycle: the two diagonal cells of a return x volume double sort. RET is 12-1 momentum, close[t-skip] over close[t-mom] - 1; RVOL is mean volume over the last vol_n bars divided by the mean over the vol_n bars before that, the OHLCV proxy for turnover. Long only quiet winners (top RET tercile AND bottom RVOL tercile), short only loud losers (bottom RET AND top RVOL); the other seven cells are flat -- the LONG leg requiring LOW relative volume is the opposite of a volume-confirmation filter and is the whole point. HONEST LIMIT: the harness is single-symbol, so a cross-sectional tercile cannot be computed. The terciles are taken against the symbol's OWN trailing rank_n-bar distribution of RET and of RVOL, which keeps the double sort and the diagonal-cell rule but makes it a time-series rather than a cross-sectional strategy. The overlapping six-vintage book becomes the harness's single position with a bar-count hold.
cut.source: Lee & Swaminathan (2000), 'Price Momentum and Trading Volume', Journal of Finance 55(5), 2017-2069 -- the momentum life cycle hypothesis and the RET x turnover double sort. RVOL is the stated OHLCV substitution for turnover.

cut.name: FLOSS Arc-Curve Segmentation
cut.note: Regime boundaries from the topology of nearest-neighbour arcs rather than from any moment of the return distribution: each finished subsequence is joined to its closest earlier match, and where the market's shape vocabulary changes almost no arc crosses, so the corrected arc curve collapses. Entry is the direction of the new regime measured against the m bars before the boundary; exit is the next boundary. Arcs are the causal backward form (a new subsequence matching the past), which is the only version knowable in real time; distances are z-normalised PAA so the whole thing stays cheap.
cut.source: Gharghabi, Ding, Yeh, Kamgar, Ulanova & Keogh, 'Matrix Profile VIII: Domain Agnostic Online Semantic Segmentation at Superhuman Performance Levels', IEEE ICDM 2017 (FLUSS offline, FLOSS online with forward-only arcs). UCR Matrix Profile page: cs.ucr.edu/~eamonn/MatrixProfile.html. Financial application survey: 'Financial Time Series: Market Analysis Techniques Based on Matrix Profiles', MDPI Engineering Proceedings 5(1):45.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Roughness Index of Log-Volatility
cut.note: Estimates the Hurst exponent of LOG-VOLATILITY (not of price) with the q=1 absolute-increment scaling m(D) ~ D^H of the rough-volatility literature, on realised volatility measured over non-overlapping blocks of bars. When vol is unusually PERSISTENT and high it follows the tape; when it is unusually ROUGH it fades a 2-ATR excursion from the mean, because a one-bar vol spike has no follow-through mechanism. The literature's absolute 0.25/0.08 cutoffs are daily-calibrated and unreachable intraday (measured H is 0.0-0.15 on every probe symbol), so the two branches are cut on H's own trailing percentile, which is what 'H drifts up toward persistence' actually means.
cut.source: Gatheral, Jaisson & Rosenbaum, 'Volatility is rough', arXiv:1410.3394, published Quantitative Finance 18(6) 2018 - opened and verified this session; confirms 'log-volatility behaves essentially as a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst exponent H of order 0.1, at any reasonable time scale' and the m(q,Delta) ~ Delta^(qH) scaling framework. The rolling-window trading application and the two-branch entry are my synthesis.

cut.name: Online Logistic Regression with Dead Band
cut.note: Eight technical features, each standardised by an EXPANDING mean/sd that only ever sees bars strictly before the current one, are fed to a logistic regression whose weights are updated by online SGD. The update is DELAYED and causally honest: the sample built at bar t is held in a queue and only learned from at bar t+hor, when its label (did the close rise over hor bars) has actually matured. Trading starts after warmup bars. The dead band is the point: long only when p > 0.5+band, short only when p < 0.5-band, silent in between, so the model abstains whenever its features disagree. Because the weights are never batch-refit they drift with the tape, and the sign of the coefficient on the momentum feature is free to flip, which is what makes one piece of code a momentum model in one regime and a reversion model in another. Exit is the same hor-bar horizon the label was defined over, plus a 2*ATR stop; a still-valid probability simply re-enters on the next bar, so a persistent signal rolls.
cut.source: Standard online SGD logistic regression. Finance instantiation with technical-indicator features and a cascaded architecture: Zhang, Zhang et al., 'Cascading logistic regression onto gradient boosted decision trees for forecasting and trading stock indices', Applied Soft Computing 84 (2019). Adaptive online mid-price learning with Hessian-based adaptive rate: PLOS ONE 15(6): e0234107, 'Mid-price prediction based on machine learning methods with technical and quantitative indicators'.
